DAMGHANI:v1p293/r16.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r16.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r16.claim: Ṭaghā can mean rising and increasing, as the water rose and overflowed.
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r16.anchor: الطغيان الارتفاع والكثرة قوله سبحانه في سورة الحاقة

NAHHAS:v5p19/r27.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r27.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r27.claim: Calling the audience carried in Noah’s Ark is figurative: their ancestors were aboard, so descendants are treated as having been carried with them.
NAHHAS:v5p19/r27.anchor: مجاز لأن الجارية سفينة نوح صلى الله عليه وسلم والمخاطبون بهذا إنما حمل أجدادهم فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.claim: A report says God sends each wind and drop of rain in measured amounts, except in Noah's and Aad's times: floodwaters overwhelmed their keepers, and Aad's wind escaped them; it cites 69:11 and 69:6.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.anchor: ما أرسل الله سفينة من ريح إلا بمكيال ولا قطرة من مطر إلا بمكيال إلا يوم عاد ويوم نوح

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r1.claim: Noah’s people are included last in the list though they were historically the first nation mentioned to face God’s wrath, briefly evoking the history of the messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r1.anchor: Historically, they were the first among those nations mentioned to have faced the wrath of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r2.claim: Quraysh are reminded that their ancestors were rescued in Noah’s ark because they believed in God’s messenger; as Noah’s descendants they indirectly received that favor and must remember history.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r2.anchor: the people whose descendents they are, were given refuge in the ark of Noah (sws) by the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r3.claim: If Quraysh forget this favor and disobey their messenger, God may deal with them as He dealt with Noah’s people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p451/r3.anchor: there is no reason why the Almighty not deal with them in the very manner He dealt with the people of Noah (sws).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r3.claim: The flood rose fifteen cubits above the world's highest mountain; Ibn Jubayr says it overpowered the flood's keepers as the wind overpowered its keepers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r3.anchor: أي زاد وعلا على أعلى جبل في الدنيا خمس عشرة ذراعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the water overpowered its keepers just as the destructive wind did.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r4.anchor: قال ابن جبير: طغى على الخزان، كما طغت الريح على خزانها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r5.claim: The plural second-person pronoun refers to later descendants carried in their forefathers' loins aboard Noah's ark; jāriyah became a common word for a ship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r5.anchor: حملناكم: أي في أصلاب آبائكم، في الجارية: هي سفينة نوح عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r6.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawī reads the phrase broadly as ships sailing, a divine favor whose human beneficiaries are the addressed audience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p256/r6.anchor: وقال المهدوي: المعنى في السفن الجارية يعني أن ذلك هو على سبيل الامتنان

RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r1.claim: One account says the water overwhelmed its keepers, who could no longer tell how much had emerged; outside that event, every drop fell in a measured amount.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r1.anchor: طغى الماء على خزانه فلم يدروا كم خرج وليس ينزل من السماء قطرة قبل تلك الواقعة ولا بعدها إلا بكيل معلوم

RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r2.speaker: سائر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r2.claim: The other commentators understand the water to have exceeded its bounds until it rose over and covered everything.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r2.anchor: وسائر المفسرين قالوا : { طغى * الماء } أي تجاوز حده حتى علا كل شيء

RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r3.claim: The people addressed are descendants of those carried in the Ark; their ancestors were carried while they were still in their loins.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r3.anchor: و { حملناكم } أي حملنا آباءكم وأنتم في أصلابهم ، ولا شك أن الذين خوطبوا بهذا هم أولاد

RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r4.claim: Al-jāriya means the ship, specifically Noah’s Ark; jāriya is a name for a ship.
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r4.anchor: وقوله : { فى الجارية } يعني في السفينة التي تجري في الماء ، وهي سفينة نوح عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p94/r5.claim: Rāzī connects the ship’s name al-jawārī with the reference to ships in 55:24.

RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: Basic derivation among related words is familiar, while greater derivation by permuting root letters is difficult; it is most workable with triliteral roots, whose permutations number six, as larger roots multiply and leave most combinations unused.
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor: الاشتقاق الأصغر سهل معتاد مألوف أما الاشتقاق الأكبر فرعايته صعبة وكأنه لا يمكن رعايته إلا في الكلمات الثلاثية

RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: Even triliteral roots rarely use all permutations, but the attainable amount of greater derivation is the highest possible achievement in linguistic inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: الكلمات الثلاثية قلما يوجد فيها ما يكون جميع تقاليبها الممكنة معتبرة بل يكون في الأكثر بعضها مستعملا وبعضها مهملا

RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: Al-Razi says five permutations of k-l-m convey force or intensity: kalām strikes ear and mind, kalm is a wound, rough land is severe, kamula means complete, lakama is a forceful punch, makūl is a difficult low-water well, and malaka means firming dough or having power.
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: تركيب الكاف واللام والميم بحسب تقاليبها الممكنة الستة تفيد القوة والشدة خمسة منها معتبرة وواحد ضائع

RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: The singular word kalima can denote connected extended speech, as when a whole poem, the testimony of faith or a good utterance is called a word.
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: لفظ الكلمة قد يستعمل في اللفظة الواحدة ويراد بها الكلام الكثير الذي قد ارتبط بعضه ببعض

RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r5.claim: Calling a compound a word is metaphor rather than homonymy: it uses a part's name for the whole, and linked speech gains a unity resembling a single word.
RAZI-FULL:v1p24/r5.anchor: لما كان المجاز أولى من الاشتراك علمنا أن إطلاق لفظ الكلمة على المركب مجاز وذلك لوجهين

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r1.claim: The overflowing waters allude to Noah’s Flood and Ark.
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r1.anchor: These verses are taken as an allusion to Noah’s Ark

STUDYQURAN:69:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r2.claim: “We carried you” means God carried the people’s forefathers while they were still in their descendants’ loins.
STUDYQURAN:69:11/r2.anchor: We carried you means We carried your forefathers while you were still in their loins

TAB-FULL:v23p220/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r1.claim: Qatāda reports that the flood rose fifteen cubits above everything.
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {إنا لما طغى الماء} [الحاقة: 11] قال: بلغنا أنه طغى فوق كل شيء خمس عشرة ذراعا

TAB-FULL:v23p220/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the flood escaped the keepers’ knowledge and control as it rose in anger at God’s command.
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية} [الحاقة: 11] قال: لم تنزل من السماء قطرة إلا بعلم الخزان، إلا حيث طغى الماء

TAB-FULL:v23p220/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ṭaghā as the water becoming abundant during the nights when Noah’s people drowned.
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنا لما طغى} [الحاقة: 11] الماء يعني كثر الماء ليالي غرق الله قوم نوح

TAB-FULL:v23p220/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r4.claim: Mujāhid’s transmitted glosses describe the water as surging or rising.
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم} [الحاقة: 11] قال محمد بن عمرو في حديثه: طما؛ وقال الحارث: ظهر

TAB-FULL:v23p220/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses ṭaghā as increasing and rising.
TAB-FULL:v23p220/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {لما طغى الماء} [الحاقة: 11] كثر وارتفع

TAB-FULL:v23p221/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p221/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p221/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-jāriya as the ship.
TAB-FULL:v23p221/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {حملناكم في الجارية} [الحاقة: 11] الجارية: السفينة

TAB-FULL:v23p221/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p221/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p221/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says this was Noah’s ship; the Qurʾān addresses later descendants, since their ancestors’ being carried counts as their being carried.
TAB-FULL:v23p221/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {حملناكم في الجارية} [الحاقة: 11] والجارية: سفينة نوح التي حملتم فيها وقيل: حملناكم

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r16.claim: The water’s transgression refers to Noah’s flood, and al-jāriya is the ship.
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r16.anchor: إشارة إلى طوفان نوح والجارية السفينة

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r17.claim: The addressed people are described as carried in Noah’s ship, although their ancestors were literally aboard, because all people belong to one kind and one group’s state can be attributed to the whole.
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r17.anchor: والمحمول في الحقيقة أسلافهم لكون الجميع نوعا واحدا ينسب حال البعض منه إلى الكل

BURSEVI:v10p103/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r1.claim: The water is the familiar floodwater of Noah's time, which exceeded its normal bounds; one report says it rose five hundred cubits above everything.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r1.anchor: تى ارتفع على كل شيء خمسمائة ذراع

BURSEVI:v10p103/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p103/r2.claim: Another report says the flood rose fifteen cubits above the highest mountain; an alternative account describes a level the angels assigned to control it could not contain.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r2.anchor: أو حده في المعاملة مع خزنة من الملائكة بحيث لم يقدروا على ضبطه

BURSEVI:v10p103/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r3.claim: The flood's excess was caused by Noah's people persisting in disbelief, sins, and denial of his revealed teachings, including matters of the Resurrection; God avenged them by drowning.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r3.anchor: بسبب إصرار قوم نوح على فنون الكفر والمعاصي ومبالغتهم في تكذيبه

BURSEVI:v10p103/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r4.claim: The people addressed are carried through their ancestors while still in their loins, so they are spoken of as personally carried; this highlights the favor, since their ancestors' rescue enabled their descendants to exist.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r4.anchor: أيها الناس أي حملنا آباءكم وأنتم في أصلابكم فكأنكم محمولون بأشخاصكم

BURSEVI:v10p103/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r5.claim: Al-Jāriya is Noah's ship, so named because it runs upon water; being carried in it means being lifted above the flood until it subsided.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r5.anchor: يعني في سفينة نوح لأن من شأنها أن تجري على الماء

BURSEVI:v10p103/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r6.claim: The preposition fī is not governed directly by ḥamalnā; it belongs to an omitted circumstantial phrase describing the carried people as protected aboard the moving ship.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r6.anchor: فإنها ليست بصلة للحمل بل متعلقة بمحذوف هو حال من مفعوله

BURSEVI:v10p103/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p103/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p103/r7.claim: Their rescue depended solely on God's protection; the ship was only an apparent, formal cause, not the true source of safety.
BURSEVI:v10p103/r7.anchor: مدار نجاتهم محض عصمته تعالى وإنما السفينة سبب صوري

TABRISI:69:12/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:12/r3.claim: Al-jāriya means a ship that sails on water and also a young woman, whose water of youth is flowing.
TABRISI:69:12/r3.anchor: الجارية السفينة التي من شأنها أن تجري على الماء والجارية المرأة الشابة

TABRISI:69:12/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:12/r16.claim: When the water exceeded its known limit and flooded the earth, God carried the ancestors of the addressed people in the ship.
TABRISI:69:12/r16.anchor: أي جاوز الحد المعروف حتى غرقت الأرض بما عليها إلا من شاء الله نجاته

TABRISI:69:12/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:69:12/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd say the people carried in the ship were the ancestors of those addressed.
TABRISI:69:12/r17.anchor: أي حملنا آباءكم في السفينة عن ابن عباس وابن زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r1.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r1.claim: In Noah’s time the water overwhelmed its keepers and swelled beyond their measure; no rain before or after that day fell except by a known measure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي عن ابن عباس: يعني: زمن نوح طغى الماء على خزانه، وكثر عليهم، فلم يدروا كم خرج،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the water grew angry at the Lord’s anger and overflowed its keepers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r2.anchor: وروي عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قال: غضب الماء لغضب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r3.speaker: سائر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r3.claim: Most commentators say the water exceeded its bounds, rose above everything, and reached fifteen cubits above it; Qatada and Muqatil are named among them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r3.anchor: وسائر المفسرين قالوا في: {طغى الماء} تجاوز حده، وخرج عن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r4.claim: God carried the addressees’ ancestors in the Ark while they were still in their loins; the present audience descends from those carried, as Muqatil and al-Kalbi also say.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r5.claim: This address to descendants parallels the verse saying that God carried their progeny.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p148/r5.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r1.claim: Al-jāriya is Noah’s ship, which sails on water; it is one of the words for a ship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r1.anchor: وقوله: {في الجارية} يعني في السفينة التي تجري في الماء، وهي سفينة نوح عليه السلام،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p149/r2.claim: The same term for ships appears in “and His are the ships sailing.”

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r11.claim: The floodwater exceeded its limit during the days of the Flood.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r11.anchor: { إنا لما طغى الماء } جاوز حده. يعني: أيام الطوفان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r12.claim: God carried the audience’s ancestors aboard Noah’s ship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:7-11/r12.anchor: { حملناكم } أي: حملنا آباءكم { في الجارية } وهي السفينة.

QASHANI:69:9-12/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:9-12/r5.claim: The overflowing water is the flood of prime matter.

QASHANI:69:9-12/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:9-12/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:9-12/r6.claim: The ark is the religious law, composed of scientific and practical perfection.
QASHANI:69:9-12/r6.anchor: في جارية الشريعة المركبة من الكمال العلمي والعملي

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r2.claim: The water's transgression refers to the time of Noah's flood.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r2.anchor: O su tuğyan ettiği vakit Yani Nûh’un tûfânı zamanında

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r3.claim: God preserved the audience in the loins of their believing ancestors while destroying the deniers, carrying their descendants forward rather than cutting off their line.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r3.anchor: tekzib eden diğerlerinin kökünü keserken sizin kökünüzü kesmedik de iman eden atalarınızın sulbünde taşıyarak muhafaza ettik.

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r4.claim: Al-jariya means the flowing vessel and, with the definite article, refers to Noah's ark; calling a ship a jariya is conventional usage, as the cited line about ninety girls in a ship illustrates.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r4.anchor: Ahd ile “el-câriye”, Hazret-i Nûh’un gemisidir. Mutlaka gemiye “câriye” ıtlâkı da müte‘âreftir.

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r5.claim: A cited poetic line says 'ninety girls in the belly of a ship,' using jariya for a vessel.

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r6.claim: The singular definite al-jariya also hints that the people addressed were then preserved in the current of their ancestors' loins along with the ark.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r6.anchor: burada yalnız “el-câriye” denilmesinde onunla beraber muhatabların o vakit orada atalarının sulbündeki bir cereyanda mahfuz bulunduklarına da bir îmâ vardır.

ELMALILI:69:10-12/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r7.claim: God, not the ark, was the true carrier and protector; the ark was an apparent means displaying divine power, and faith was the spiritual reason for boarding.
ELMALILI:69:10-12/r7.anchor: Ona yüklemenin sebeb-i mânevîsi de iman idi. Hakīkī fâil ise Biz idik.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r5.claim: The event in verse 11 is the flood in Noah's time: his rebellious people drowned, while the believers who boarded his ark survived.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r5.anchor: Nûh kavmi peygambere isyan etmelerinin cezasını tufanda boğularak çekmişler, Nûh’a inanıp onun gemisine binenler ise kurtulmuşlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r6.claim: The “you” carried in the ark refers to the believers saved by God's grace, who came ashore after the waters receded and became ancestors of later generations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:9/r6.anchor: o gün Nûh’un gemisinde bulunup da Allah’ın lutfuyla kurtuluşa eren, sular çekildikten sonra da karaya çıkan

BURHAN:v3p439/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p439/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p439/r3.claim: طغى literally means rose, but conveys more forcefully that the flood rose in a conquering, overwhelming way.
BURHAN:v3p439/r3.anchor: لأن حقيقة طغى علا والاستعارة أبلغ لأن طغى علا قاهرا

BURHAN:v3p442/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p442/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p442/r14.claim: In the flood verse, the source of the metaphor is arrogance and its target is water; their shared feature is excessive rising.
BURHAN:v3p442/r14.anchor: المستعار منه التكبر والمستعار له الماء والجامع الاستعلاء المفرط

ITQAN:v3p121/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p121/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p121/r6.claim: In describing the water's excess, the abstract idea of arrogance is borrowed for perceptible abundance; the common feature is elevation.
ITQAN:v3p121/r6.anchor: المستعار منه التكبر وهو عقلي والمستعار له كثرة الماء وهو حسي والجامع الاستعلاء

SULAMI:v2p347#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p347#3/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p347#3/r1.claim: Bodies did not yet exist and spirits cannot bear the current; rather, it is the Real flowing upon them according to appointed divisions, a mystery recognized when the spirit beholds these stations.
SULAMI:v2p347#3/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : الأجسام لم تكن والأرواح لا تحمل الجاري إنما هو جريان الحق عليه بشرط الأقسام

SULAMI:v2p347#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p347#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p347#3/r2.claim: God touched one side of Adam and brought out his descendants; He carried humanity by His signs and allotted its times according to His measures.
SULAMI:v2p347#3/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : مسح أحد شقى آدم وأخرج منه الذرية . قال : حملناكم بشواهدنا وأجرينا لكم الأوقات

ITQAN:v4p351/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r1.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v4p351/r1.claim: Swearing by created things entails an oath by their Creator, since an effect cannot exist without an agent.
ITQAN:v4p351/r1.anchor: وقال ابن أبي الإصبع في أسرار الفواتح القسم بالمصنوعات يستلزم القسم بالصانع لأن ذكر المفعول يستلزم ذكر الفاعل

ITQAN:v4p351/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r2.speaker: الحسن
ITQAN:v4p351/r2.claim: God may swear by whatever He wills, but people may swear only by God.
ITQAN:v4p351/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن قال إن الله يقسم بما شاء من خلقه وليس لأحد أن يقسم إلا بالله

ITQAN:v4p351/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r3.speaker: العلماء
ITQAN:v4p351/r3.claim: The divine oath by the Prophet’s life teaches people his great rank and standing with God.
ITQAN:v4p351/r3.anchor: وقال العلماء أقسم الله تعالى بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله ﴿ لعمرك ﴾ لتعرف الناس عظمته عند الله ومكانته لديه

ITQAN:v4p351/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p351/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Muhammad was the most honored person God created and that God swore by no one else’s life.
ITQAN:v4p351/r4.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال ما خلق الله ولا ذرأ ولا برأ نفسا أكرم عليه من محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v4p351/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r5.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
ITQAN:v4p351/r5.claim: Al-Qushayri says oaths are by something for its excellence, as with Sinai and the secure city, or benefit, as with the fig and olive.
ITQAN:v4p351/r5.anchor: وقال أبو القاسم القشيري القسم بالشيء لا يخرج عن وجهين إما لفضيلة أو لمنفعة فالفضيلة

ITQAN:v4p351/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p351/r6.claim: Another classification divides divine oaths into those by God’s essence, His acts, and His created objects.
ITQAN:v4p351/r6.anchor: وقال غيره أقسم الله تعالى بثلاثة أشياء بذاته كالآيات السابقة وبفعله نحو

ITQAN:v4p351/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p351/r7.claim: Oaths may be explicit or implicit; an implicit oath may be signaled by lām or inferred from meaning, with “By God” understood.
ITQAN:v4p351/r7.anchor: والقسم إما ظاهر كالآيات السابقة وإما مضمر وهو قسمان قسم دلت عليه اللام نحو

ITQAN:v4p351/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p351/r8.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ITQAN:v4p351/r8.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi distinguishes expressions that may be ordinary reports or oaths from forms that take an oath response.
ITQAN:v4p351/r8.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي الألفاظ الجارية مجرى القسم ضربان أحدهما ما تكون كغيرها من الأخبار التي ليست بقسم فلا تجاب بجوابه

ITQAN:v2p334#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p334#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p334#3/r1.claim: The water’s ṭughyān means it became abundant or overflowed.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r1.claim: Those who reject poetry study deprive themselves of wisdom and broad learning; they should first examine whether they have mastered the disciplines they accept as necessary for interpretation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r1.anchor: ومنعتموها الاطلاع على مدارج الحكمة وعلى العلوم الجمة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r2.claim: A predicate may be a single word or a clause, and a single-word predicate may or may not contain a pronoun referring back to its subject.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r3.claim: A predicate clause has four forms and must contain a reference to its subject; that reference can be omitted in wording when context supplies it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r3.anchor: وأنه لا بد لكل جملة وقعت خبرا لمبتدأ من أن يكون فيها ذكر يعود إلى المبتدأ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r4.claim: Adjectives can restrict or clarify a noun, and these functions differ; generality is also distinct from ambiguity.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r4.anchor: كما أن فائدة الشياع غير فائدة الإبهام

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r5.claim: An adjective may reinforce an established meaning, as in أمس الدابر or the Quranic phrase نفخة واحدة, or serve praise; these functions are not restriction or clarification.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r5.anchor: وصفة يراد بها المدح والثناء كالصفات الجارية على اسم الله تعالى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r6.claim: An adjective, a predicate, and a circumstantial expression all attribute a meaning to something, but differ in how they establish that relation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p43/r6.anchor: وهل عرفتم الفرق بين الصفة والخبر

RUMMANI:v1p87/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p87/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p87/r2.claim: Overflowed literally means rose; as metaphor it intensifies the scene by making the water rise as an overpowering force.
RUMMANI:v1p87/r2.anchor: وقال عز وجل: {إنما لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية}. حقيقته علا والاستعارة أبلغ لأن طغى علا قاهرا

DAMGHANI:v1p143/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p143/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p143/r10.claim: Ḥaml can mean boarding people on ships and saving them; the source also cites Noah’s vessel and being carried on land and sea.
DAMGHANI:v1p143/r10.anchor: الحمل يعني الإركاب على السفن قوله تعالى في سورة الحاقة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r5.claim: Another sense is transgression or overflow, used of the water that rose before the Ark.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r5.anchor: والثاني : العصيان . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحاقة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r1.claim: Qatl is an act leading to death; qitāl is the person or life struck, and fatal points are called maqātil.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r1.anchor: القتل : الفعل المؤدي إلى الموت . والقتال النفس . تقول قتلت فلانا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r2.claim: Figuratively, killing something with knowledge means knowing it thoroughly; killing wine with water means mixing it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r2.anchor: ويقال [ قتلت ] الشيء علما ، وقتلت الخمر بالماء : مزجتها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r3.claim: Qatl can mean enemy; the poem uses aqtaal for enemies.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r4.claim: A girl’s taqattil can mean acting yielding toward a man until he falls in love.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r4.anchor: ويقال : تقتلت الجارية للرجل حتى عشقها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r5.claim: A maqtal heart is one struck down by love, as in the verse cited from Imruʾ al-Qays.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r5.anchor: ويقال : قلب مقتل ، إذا قتله العشق . قال امرؤ القيس

SAMIN-DURR:69:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:11/r1.claim: جارية became conventional usage for a ship, illustrated by a riddle about ninety ships inside a ship and the Quranic reference to ships at sea.
SAMIN-DURR:69:11/r1.anchor: قوله: { في الجارية }: غلب استعمال " الجارية " في السفينة كقوله

ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r7.claim: The vessel called al-jāriya is Noah's ship.
ZAJJAJ:v5p214#2/r7.anchor: ومعنى الجارية، أي سفينة نوح عليه السلام

ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n6/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n6/r1.claim: In the consensus of classical commentators, 'you' refers metonymically to your ancestors.
ASAD-NOTES:69:11#n6/r1.anchor: metonymically (in the consensus of all classical commentators), "your ancestors"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r1.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r1.claim: Al-Rummānī divides Qur’anic endings into those with identical final letters and those with neighboring letters, giving examples of each.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r1.anchor: والفواصل عند "الرماني" علة وجهين: أحدهما على الحروف المتجانسة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r2.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r2.claim: For al-Rummānī, meaning governs the endings, though sound and rhythmic harmony also contribute; endings mark pauses and beautify speech through patterning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r2.anchor: والفائدة في الفواصل دلالتها على المقاطع، وتحسينها الكلام بالتشاكل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r3.speaker: أبو هلال العسكري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r3.claim: Most rhetoricians resisted separating Qur’anic endings from sajʿ; Abū Hilāl al-ʿAskarī says Qur’anic patterned prose surpasses human examples in meaning, clarity, and elegance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p258/r3.anchor: بأن جميع ما في القرآن مما يجرى على التسجيع والازدواج، مخالف في تمكين المعنى وصفاء اللفظ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313/r1.claim: Qatāda says it had reached them that the floodwater rose fifteen cubits above everything.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p313/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إنا لما طغى الماء ﴾ قال بلغنا أنه طغا فوق كل شيء خمسة عشر ذراعا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.claim: ʿAlī reports that water and wind ordinarily came by measured allotment through angels, but Noah’s flood and ʿĀd’s wind were released beyond their keepers; the Ṣaḥīḥayn and others corroborate it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه قال لم تنزل قطرة إلا بمكيال على يدي ملك إلا يوم نوح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r1.claim: The water exceeded its normal bounds, rising fifteen cubits above the highest mountain.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r1.anchor: جاوز حده المعتاد حتى أنه علا على أعلى جبل خمس عشرة ذراعا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the water overwhelmed its keepers, as related just before.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r2.anchor: أو طغى على خزانه على ما سمعت قبيل هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r3.claim: The flood followed Noah’s people’s persistence in varied unbelief and sins and their intense denial of his revelations, including matters of the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r3.anchor: وذلك بسبب إصرار قوم نوح عليه السلام على فنون الكفر والمعاصي ومبالغتهم في تكذيبه عليه السلام فيما أوحي إليه من الأحكام التي من جملتها أحوال القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r4.claim: The audience were carried in their fathers’ loins.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r5.claim: Alternatively, “We carried you” means “We carried your ancestors while you were in their loins,” with an omitted possessive.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r5.anchor: أو حملنا آباءكم وأنتم في أصلابهم على أنه بتقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r6.claim: A further explanation addresses descendants as their ancestors through indwelling; Al-Ālūsī considers this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r6.anchor: وقيل على التجوز في المخاطبين بإرادة آبائهم المحمولين بعلاقة الحلول وهو بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r7.claim: The ark is Noah’s ship; carrying the audience in it means raising them above the water and preserving them through the flood, not merely boarding them.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r7.anchor: في سفينة نوح عليه السلام والمراد بحملهم فيها رفعهم فوق الماء إلى انقضاء أيام الطوفان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r8.claim: The preposition “in” is not governed by “carried”; it belongs to an omitted circumstantial phrase describing them as kept safe aboard the moving ship.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r8.anchor: فإنها ليست بصلة للحمل بل متعلقة بمحذوف هو حال من مفعوله أي رفعناكم فوق الماء وحفظناكم حال كونكم في السفينة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r9.claim: Their rescue depended solely on God’s protection; the ship was only an outward means.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r9.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على أن مدار نجاتهم محض عصمته عز وجل وإنما السفينة سبب صوري

ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p42#5/r10.claim: Jāriya is commonly used for a ship, as illustrated by “ninety maidens in the belly of a maiden.”

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r25.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r25.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r25.claim: The water transgressed its limit and rose above everything during Noah's time.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r25.anchor: أي عتا وجاوز حده حتى علا على كل شيء وارتفع فوقه، يعني زمن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209/r1.claim: God carried the ancestors of those addressed, while they were still in their ancestors' loins, aboard the ship moving through the water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p209/r1.anchor: في السفينة التي تجري في الماء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r1.claim: The floodwater exceeded its normal limit or overwhelmed its keepers; it occurred in Noah's Flood and supports the preceding account.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r1.anchor: جاوز حده المعتاد، أو طغى على خزانه وذلك في الطوفان وهو يؤيد من قبله

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r2.claim: God carried the audience's ancestors, with the audience still in their loins.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:11-12/r3.anchor: في سفينة نوح عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r6.claim: The account of Noah answers the apparent question about “those before him”: God destroyed all opponents and saved all who agreed with the messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r6.anchor: أشار إلى أنه أهلك جميع المخالفين وأنجى جميع الموافقين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r7.claim: The water exceeded its bounds and rose above the highest mountain, drowning those there; people could neither control it nor resist it, beyond ordinary natural causes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r7.anchor: فزاد عن الحد حتى علا على أعلى جبل في الأرض بقدر ما يغرق من كان عليه حين أغرقنا قوم نوح عليه السلام به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r8.claim: God carried the present audience through their ancestors, by His greatness, will, and power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r8.anchor: حملناكم } أي في ظهور آبائكم بعظمتنا ومشيئتنا وقدرتنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r9.claim: “The running one” is the ark, described by its quality instead of its noun and made so exceptional that it seemed the only vessel sailing on normally drowning water.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r9.anchor: أي السفينة التي جعلناها بحكمتنا عريقة في الجريان حتى كأنه لا جارية غيرها على وجه الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r10.claim: Noah was the first to build a ship, doing so through God’s revelation and protection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p124/r10.anchor: ونوح عليه السلام أول من صنع السفينة , وإنما صنعها بوحي الله تعالى وبحفظه له

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r1.claim: Everyone on earth, human and nonhuman, drowned except those in the ark.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r1.anchor: وأغرقنا سوى من في السفينة من جميع أهل الأرض من أدمي وغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r2.claim: God instructed Noah to shape the ark like a bird’s breast so its movement in water would resemble movement through air.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r2.anchor: اجعلها كهيئة صدر الطائر ليكون ما يجري في الماء مقاربا لما يجري في الهواء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.claim: The narrative starts with Thamūd as the nearest destroyed people to Mecca, since nearby warnings are more forceful, and ends with Noah’s people, who covered the earth and were known to all later people.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p125/r3.anchor: بدأ سبحانه وتعالى بثمود الذين هم أقرب المهلكين إلى مكة المشرفة لأن التخويف بالأقرب أقعد

DURR-FULL:v8p264/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that rain and wind were normally measured by their keepers, but Noah's flood overwhelmed them; likewise, ʿĀd's wind overwhelmed its keepers and is called dominant.
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما أنزل الله من السماء كفا من ماء إلا بمكيال

DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.speaker: قبيصة بن ذؤيب
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.claim: Qubayṣa ibn Dhūʾayb says wind-keepers normally know every wind's measure, but ʿĀd's wind escaped their knowledge in God's anger, so it was called defiant; Noah's water similarly became overflowing.
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.anchor: من طريق ابن شهاب عن قبيصة بن ذؤيب قال: ما يخرج من الريح شيء إلا عليها خزان يعلمون قدرها وعددها

DURR-FULL:v8p265/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r13.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r13.claim: Mujāhid explains the water's ṭughyān as its becoming abundant or overflowing.
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r13.anchor: وفي قوله: {إنا لما طغى الماء} قال: كثر

DURR-FULL:v8p265/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r14.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r14.claim: Mujāhid explains al-jāriya as the ship.
DURR-FULL:v8p265/r14.anchor: وفي قوله: {حملناكم في الجارية} قال: السفينة

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the flood exceeded its keepers: ordinarily rain fell by measured weight, but in Noah's time it overflowed without measure.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنا لما طغى الماء} قال: طغى على خزانه فنزل ولم ينزل من السماء ماء

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says every raindrop was known to its keepers except during the flood, when God's anger caused it to overwhelm them in an unmeasured quantity.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: لم ينزل من السماء قطرة قط إلا بعلم الخزان إلا حيث طغى الماء

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r3.claim: Qatāda reports that the flood rose fifteen cubits above everything.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {طغى الماء} قال: بلغني أنه طغى فوق كل شيء خمسة عشر ذراعا

DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the jāriya as the ship; its survival is a reminder of Noah's people punished for disobeying him, and an aware ear preserves the ship's story.
DURR-FULL:v8p266/r4.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {حملناكم في الجارية} قال: السفينة وفي قوله: {لنجعلها لكم تذكرة} أي تذكرون ماصنع بهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.claim: Recalling Noah’s people embeds gratitude for all people descended from the group saved from the flood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r4.anchor: حسن اقتضاب التذكير بأخذهم لما فيه من إدماج امتنان على جميع الناس الذين تناسلوا من الفئة الذين نجاهم الله من الغرق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r5.claim: The famous time of Noah’s flood is treated as known and made the temporal condition for “when We carried you in the vessel.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r5.anchor: فجعل شرطا ل { لما } في قوله : { إنا لما طغا الماء حملناكم في الجارية }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r6.claim: Water’s “transgression” is a near metaphor for its unprecedented force, likened to a tyrant overstepping against people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r6.anchor: والطغيان : مستعار لشدته الخارقة للعادة تشبيها لها بطغيان الطاغي على الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r7.claim: Al-jāriya describes an omitted ship, safīna; the description became almost its name, as in 55:24.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r7.anchor: و { الجارية } : صفة لمحذوف وهو السفينة وقد شاع هذا الوصف حتى صار بمنزلة الاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r8.claim: Ḥaml originally means placing one body on another to move it; here it extends metaphorically to placing people in a moving vessel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r8.anchor: أطلق هنا على الوضع في ظرف متنقل على وجه الاستعارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r9.claim: Attributing the carrying to God is a grammatical metaphor: God instructed Noah to build the vessel and place the passengers aboard, as in 23:27.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p122/r9.anchor: وإسناد الحمل إلى اسم الجلالة مجاز عقلي بناء على أنه أوحى إلى نوح بصنع الحاملة ووضع المحمول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r14.claim: The water’s excess occurred in Noah’s flood; it crossed customary bounds, overwhelming its keepers and drowning people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r14.anchor: والمراد: طغى الماء في وقت الطوفان الذي كان على قوم نوح. والطغيان: الزيادة على الحدود المتعارفة في الأشياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r15.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r15.claim: Qatada says the floodwater rose fifteen cubits above everything.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p357#2/r15.anchor: قال قتادة: علا على كل شيء خمسة عشر ذراعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.claim: The author points to listeners and critics distinguishing individual poets’ styles, then says he omits many such examples for brevity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.anchor: ألا ترى ميز الجارية نفس الأعشى وميز الفرزدق نفس جرير من نفس ذي الرمة ونظر الأعرابي في قوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.claim: The Quran’s challenge to produce a comparable surah made eloquent Arabs test its uniqueness; like al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, they recognized it was neither poetry, soothsaying, nor madness and knew no human could match it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.anchor: قال كل فصيح في نفسه: وما بال هذا الكلام حتى لا آتي بمثله؟ فلما تأمله وتدبره، ميز منه ما ميز الوليد بن المغيرة حين قال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.claim: Some accepted the Quran, while envious opponents such as Abū Jahl resorted to fighting and bloodshed because they could not meet its challenge; ultimately the Arabs entered Islam and no tribe openly remained unbelieving at the Prophet’s death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.anchor: فمنهم من آمن وأذعن، ومنهم من حسد كأبي جهل وغيره ففر إلى القتال، ورضي بسفك الدم عجزا عن المعارضة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.claim: The Quran’s challenge proves the message to all humanity through the Arabs, its foremost eloquent speakers; God made each prophet’s miracle excel in the field most advanced in that era—magic for Moses, medicine for Jesus, and eloquence for Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.anchor: وقامت الحجة على العالم بالعرب إذ كانوا أرباب الفصاحة ومظنة المعارضة، كما قامت الحجة في معجزة عيسى بالأطباء، وفي معجزة موسى بالسحرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r1.claim: In Noah's time, the water overflowed its bounds until it covered everything.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r1.anchor: إنا لما طغى الماء أي تجاوز حده حتى علا على كل شيء في زمن نوح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r2.claim: “We carried you” means that God carried your ancestors, with you still in their loins, aboard the ship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p348#2/r2.anchor: حملناكم يعني حملنا آباءكم وأنتم في أصلابهم في الجارية وهي السفينة التي تجري في الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r11.claim: The water transgressed its limit by God's permission and rose beyond the land.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r11.anchor: ثم قال الله تعالى: {إنا لما طغى الماء} أي: زاد على الحد بإذن الله وارتفع على الوجود.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas and others gloss طغى الماء as the water becoming abundant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: {طغى الماء} كثر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r13.claim: The flood followed Noah's supplication against people who denied him and worshipped other gods; it engulfed the earth except those with Noah in the Ark, and humanity descends from Noah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: {طغى الماء} كثر -وذلك بسبب دعوة نوح، عليه السلام، على قومه حين كذبوه وخالفوه، فعبدوا غير الله فاستجاب الله له وعم أهل الأرض بالطوفان إلا من كان مع نوح في السفينة، فالناس كلهم من سلالة نوح وذريته.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.claim: ʿAli reports that water and wind were normally measured by angels; on Noah's day water was released beyond its reservoirs and overflowed, while on ʿĀd's day the wind was released and exceeded its keepers' control.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: لم تنزل قطرة من ماء إلا بكيل على يدي ملك، فلما كان يوم نوح أذن للماء دون الخزان

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r8.claim: Ṭughyān is crossing a limit; the water exceeded its normal height until it drowned the earth and its inhabitants.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r8.anchor: الطغيان: مجاوزة الحد، وطغى الماء: جاوز الحد المعروف في العظم حتى غرق الأرض ومن فيها.

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r9.claim: Al-jāriya means a ship because it moves over water; a young woman is also called jāriya because youthful beauty flows in her.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r9.anchor: والجارية: السفينة سميت لجريانها على الماء، والجارية؛ لأنها يجري فيها ماء الشباب.

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r8.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r8.claim: The flood exceeded its limit and rose fifteen cubits above everything, according to Qatada.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: طغى فوق كل شيء خمس عشرة ذراعا،

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid are cited for the alternative that the flood rose even higher than fifteen cubits.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r9.anchor: وقيل: أكثر، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد.

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r10.claim: The addressees are Noah’s ancestors: descendants are addressed with gratitude for favors to their fathers and with their ancestors’ praise or blame.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r10.anchor: حملناكم أي: حملنا آباءكم؛ لأن الابن يخاطب بالشكر على ما أسدى إلى أبيه

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd explain al-jāriya as the ship.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r11.anchor: في الجارية أي: السفينة، عن ابن عباس، وابن زيد،

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r12.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r12.claim: Al-Hasan gives the ship’s dimensions as 1,300 cubits long and 600 wide, sailing between waters.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r12.anchor: وقيل: طول السفينة ألف وثلاثمائة ذراع، وعرضها ستمائة ذراع تجري بين المائين، عن الحسن.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r7.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Najih glosses the water as having appeared.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r7.anchor: أحدها : ظهر , رواه ابن أبي نجيح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r8.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r8.claim: Ata says the water increased and grew abundant.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r9.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r9.claim: Ali says the water overflowed its angelic keepers in anger for their Lord, and they could not restrain it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r9.anchor: الثالث : أنه طغى على خزانه من الملائكة , غضبا لربه فلم يقدروا على حبسه , قاله علي رضي الله عنه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r10.claim: Qatada says the water rose fifteen cubits above everything.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r10.anchor: قال قتادة : زاد على كل شيء خمسة عشر ذراعا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says wind and rain normally arrive in measured amounts, but Noah's flood overwhelmed its angelic keepers, and Aad's wind overwhelmed its keepers; he cites 69:6-7.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r11.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال : ما أرسل من ريح قط إلا بمكيال . وما أنزل الله من قطرة قط إلا بمثقال , إلا يوم نوح وعاد ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r12.claim: The vessel is Noah's ark, called a running ship because it sails on water.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r12.anchor: يعني سفينة نوح , سميت بذلك لأنها جارية على الماء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r13.claim: The addressees were carried as ancestors through the forefathers from whom they descend.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r13.anchor: أحدهما : حملنا آباءكم الذين أنتم من ذريتهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r14.claim: Alternatively, they were carried within their forefathers' loins and thus counted among those carried; al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib's poem supports this view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r14.anchor: الثاني : أنهم في ظهور آبائهم المحمولين , فصاروا معهم , وقد قال العباس بن عبد المطلب ما يدل على هذا الوجه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r15.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r15.claim: Al-Abbas's poem traces the Prophet through the loins of his ancestors to the time when Nuh's ship sailed and Nusr and his people drowned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p79/r15.anchor: بل نطفة تركب السفين وقد … ألجم نسرا وأهله الغرق .

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r15.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r15.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r15.claim: The floodwater rose forty cubits above everything.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r15.anchor: { إنا لما طغا المآء } وارتفع فوق كل شىء أربعين ذارعا

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r16.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r16.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r16.claim: The people addressed were carried in the Ark through their forefathers, while they themselves were still in those ancestors’ loins.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r16.anchor: { حملناكم في الجارية } [آية: 11] يعني السفينة يقول: حملنا الآباء وأنتم في أصلابهم في السفينة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#7/r1.claim: At the Flood, the water rose fifteen cubits above the highest mountain in the world.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#7/r1.anchor: ارتفع وقت الطوفان على أعلى جبل في الدنيا خمسة عشر ذراعا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#7/r2.claim: “We carried you” addresses your ancestors, whom God carried in Noah's Ark.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports from the Prophet that winds and water drops are normally measured, except the wind on Aad's day and water on Noah's day: each overwhelmed its angelic keepers. The report quotes 69:11 and 69:6.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.anchor: روى سفيان الثوري عن موسى بن المسيب عن شهر بن حوشب عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r1.claim: Ṭaghā means that the water rose and exceeded its bounds.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r2.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r2.claim: Ali says the flood overflowed against its angelic keepers out of zeal for their Lord, and they could not restrain it.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r2.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه: طغى على خزانه من الملائكة غضبا لربه فلم يقدروا على حبسه.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r3.claim: Qatada says the water rose fifteen cubits above everything.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: زاد على كل شيء خمسة عشر ذراعا.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Noah's flood overwhelmed its keepers, who could not tell how much escaped; except for that day, every drop before and after was measured. Qurtubi says a marfuʿ version appeared earlier in the sura.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: طغى الماء زمن نوح على خزانه فكثر عليهم فلم يدروا كم خرج. وليس من الماء قطرة تنزل قبله ولا بعده إلا بكيل معلوم

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.claim: The stories of destroyed peoples warn this community against disobeying the Messenger; God favors them as descendants of the rescued, carried in their ancestors' loins.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r5.anchor: والمقصود من قصص هذه الأمم وذكر ما حل بهم من العذاب: زجر هذه الأمة عن الاقتداء بهم في معصية الرسول. ثم من عليهم بأن جعلهم ذرية من نجا من الغرق

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.claim: 'We carried you' means God carried their ancestors while the present audience remained in their loins.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r6.anchor: { حملناكم } أي حملنا آباءكم وأنتم في أصلابهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.claim: Al-jāriya means sailing ships; Noah, his children, and all earth's people descended from those aboard were carried in them.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:11-12/r7.anchor: { في الجارية } أي في السفن الجارية. والمحمول في الجارية نوح وأولاده، وكل من على وجه الأرض من نسل أولئك.
